_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::level_set#3 and a FALSIFICATION of the magnitude in its Signal. The rule (SUPG with DEFINITION_TAU: Taylor_Hughes_Zarins is the right default for advection-dominated level-set transport) is confirmed by the upstream deck levelset_gaussian_hill_pbc, which relies on exactly that default. But 'ringing across element edges (5-10% amplitude that does not damp)' is not what happens: STABTYPE: no_stabilization on that deck completes normally, produces no NaN, fails all four pinned phi values, and every one of those deviations is below 1% of the reference -- none exceeds 5%. So the unstabilised run is wrong, but quietly and by a small amount, detectable only against a reference solution rather than by looking for visible oscillations. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf).

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: leave the deck on its default SUPG stabilisation. All four failures vanish and the deviation counts stop being measurable, so the fixture must go red.
_mutation.from: sed 's|^SCALAR TRANSPORT DYNAMIC:|SCALAR TRANSPORT DYNAMIC/STABILIZATION:\n  STABTYPE: "no_stabilization"\nSCALAR TRANSPORT DYNAMIC:|' "$BASE" > "$TMP/nostab.yaml"
